messages:
jordan (support): FYI got an escalation from ACME — their service started seeing intermittent 401s for our API around 10:22 UTC. Error from client: 'invalid signature'. They said this started right after the key rotation on their side. pinging sec + sre to triage.

acme_infra_engineer: yep, we rotated a signing key ~10:20. Tokens issued after rotation sometimes succeed, sometimes fail. We can reproduce: some requests return 200, many 401 with 'invalid signature'.

maya (sec-eng): thanks — a few quick asks: can you paste the full WWW-Authenticate/response body and the token header (just the JOSE header)? Also what's your jwks_uri and any caching proxy in front of your token verifier?

acme_infra_engineer: here's the header from a failing token: `{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"k-new-2026"}`. Our jwks endpoint is `https://acme-idp.example/.well-known/jwks.json`. No proxy on our side, but we do have a cloud CDN in front of our JWKS that caches 60s.

ravi (sre): hmm intermittent suggests cache TTL or race during rotation. Do we see kid mismatch in our logs? jordan, can you share the Redwood auth logs (jwt verification path) for the request ids?

jordan (support): pasted two request ids in thread: req_9a1f and req_9a2b. From our logs: both had kid=k-new-2026 in token header, but our JWKS cache had only keys [k-old-2024, k-old-2025] for some backend instances; others refreshed and returned k-new-2026 -> verified. Error lines: `signature verification failed: no matching public key for kid k-new-2026` and sometimes `jwks fetch 200 ok`.

maya (sec-eng): that matches a stale-JWKS-cache race. Two things to check: (1) clock skew — if tokens are signed with iat/nbf far in future, some verifiers reject; (2) algorithm/alg header mismatch during rotation (client accidentally started signing with a different alg). But logs show kid mismatch specifically. Do we have our JWKS caching TTL and refresh strategy documented?

ravi (sre): looking at the runtime: we cache JWKS for 5m in the serving layer but we have a background refresh every 60s per instance. On rotation events, if the IDP updates JWKS and CDN caches the JWKS for 60s, some instances will keep an old response until TTL expires -> intermittent. We should add a cache-busting on 4xx signature errors to force JWKS refetch.

maya (sec-eng): agreed. Also implement a fallback: when kid not found, try refetching JWKS immediately (once) and retry verification. If still missing, log with sampling and alert.

jordan (support): ACME wants an immediate workaround. Is there a quick repro we can give them to prove it's our caching?

ravi (sre): yes — here's a repro curl that hits the same code path and forces a cache miss/refetch sequence. Run this repeatedly while rotating the key at the IDP side.

```
# repro: hit our verify endpoint with bearer token
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <JWT_WITH_NEW_KID>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

ravi (sre): then tail the verifier logs on an instance that hasn't refreshed yet. You'll see the 'no matching public key' error, then after another process refreshes JWKS you'll see success. If the CDN is the source of lag, clear CDN cache or lower TTL.

acme_infra_engineer: we can purge CDN but want to avoid doing that in prod mid-rotation. Is there something you can do on Redwood side?

maya (sec-eng): short-term: I'll patch the verifier to do an immediate JWKS re-fetch on kid-miss and retry the verification once. Medium-term: add a metric and alert for 'jwks_kid_mismatch' and a runbook. Also reduce default CDN-cached TTL expectations in docs.

ops-bot: deploy queued by maya (sec-eng) — CI job 4821 started :gear:

deploy-bot: job 4821 succeeded — canary to 3 nodes :white_check_mark:

ravi (sre): patched canary is up. It now calls jwks refresh on kid-miss and logs the refetch. Jordan, can you coordinate a short window to test with ACME?

jordan (support): scheduled a brief test window at 11:05 UTC, ACME will rotate again in staging.

acme_infra_engineer: testing now against staging — first few requests failed, then after ~12s we started getting 200s consistently. Looks fixed in staging. Thanks.

maya (sec-eng): two follow-ups I already created: (1) PR to add immediate-refetch-on-kid-miss + unit tests, (2) runbook and metric pipeline: `jwks.kid_mismatch` counter + alert if >5 per 5m. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/jwks-rotation.

jordan (support): closing loop with ACME and offering them option to purge CDN for full immediate consistency. They're happy with our fix but asked for a post-mortem explaining timeline and mitigations. I'll write a short incident summary.

maya (sec-eng): add also a check in our auth telemetry to surface 'token.kid not found' with client_kid and current_jwks_kids (sampled) to speed future triage.

ravi (sre): also added a small NTP drift check on instances — if system clock off by >5s we log and alert; rare but can bite during rotation when tokens have narrow nbf windows.

acme_infra_engineer: thanks all. one question — what about signature algorithm errors? we saw one token earlier that had `alg":"HS256"` in header by mistake.

maya (sec-eng): reject HS256 for tokens that expect RS256 — we already log an 'alg mismatch' and reject. For customer-facing runbook we'll note common pitfalls: kid race, CDN TTL, alg mismatch, and clock skew.

jordan (support): incident summary draft: 1) timeline, 2) root cause = JWKS CDN TTL + per-instance JWKS cache race during customer key rotation, 3) mitigation = immediate refetch on kid-miss rolled to canary -> prod, 4) long-term = metrics + runbook + doc update, 5) optional action for customers = purge JWKS CDN or schedule rotation during off-peak. I'll put draft in #incidents channel and ping oncall for review. :thumbsup:

maya (sec-eng): thanks team. adding labels and will follow up with PR numbers in the runbook.

acme_infra_engineer: confirmed production rotation scheduled for 01:00 UTC tomorrow. We'll coordinate with Redwood during that window.

jordan (support): thanks — marking this resolved for now, will reopen if we see new errors. :white_check_mark:
